title: Peace: a reported seizure, a circulating account, and an institutional record

timeline.title: Reported seizure of the brig Peace
timeline.observation: They attribute news to Captain Whitney of Maria and identify Peace, Captain Samuel Allen, Dover–Surinam via Cayenne. The date of seizure is not supplied.
timeline.boundary: Reported event, not an independently verified court finding.

timeline.title: Providence dateline
timeline.source: Dateline printed above H012 and X016
timeline.observation: Both carry Providence, May 13. This is distinct from their publication dates.
timeline.boundary: An internal dateline does not by itself identify the original newspaper or the seizure date.

timeline.title: Gazette of the United States
timeline.observation: Prints the seizure account, attributed to Whitney, including the $25,000 valuation and claimed British-port pretext.
timeline.boundary: Earliest version currently admitted to this case record; not necessarily the first publication.

timeline.title: New Hampshire Gazette
timeline.observation: Prints corresponding text and additional commentary attributed to Mercury about a bill demanded for remitted funds.
timeline.boundary: Direct copying from H012 is unproven. The annotation itself is not independently confirmed.

timeline.title: Secretary of State report
timeline.observation: The report explains the use of two Philadelphia newspapers to supplement missing official records. Its annex lists Peace and explicitly cites Gazette of the United States, May 18.
timeline.boundary: The report documents an institutional use of newspaper evidence, not an independent adjudication of Peace.

timeline.title: Report transmitted to the House
timeline.observation: Adams transmits the collection in response to the House resolution of June 10, according to the printed covering message.
timeline.boundary: The collection concerns many captures. It does not establish that this particular story caused the request or a policy change.

timeline.title: Cayenne decree translation and accusation
timeline.observation: A translated decree and editorial allegation concern Cayenne and newspaper accounts.
timeline.boundary: The original decree and itemized eight allegations remain missing. No verified legal link to Peace is assigned.

timeline.title: Adjudication, repayment or return
timeline.observation: No case-matched independent judgment, repayment or release record has been admitted.
timeline.boundary: Unknown is not evidence that nothing happened. The institutional report is not the resolution of the case.

timeline.title: American State Papers, Foreign Relations, volume 2
timeline.observation: The consulted compilation was published in 1832 and reproduces the dated 1797 documents.
timeline.boundary: Do not label the compilation itself as a newspaper publication in June 1797.

review: Newly inspected the full scans of ASP printed pp.28–29 (PDF pp.32–33); prior admitted newspaper crops and explicit citation retained. No independent second reader.
search: See peace_search.json and peace_search_review.json for the additional 1796–1805 corpus search.

sources.pages: Printed 28–29, 57, 60, 62; title page for compilation year

unresolved_identity_leads.title: Peace, Allen, of Providence, listed at Surinam on June 11
unresolved_identity_leads.note: The scan supports the name, master surname, home port and Surinam listing. This is a plausible continuation lead; it neither states a release from Cayenne nor establishes the identity beyond doubt.

unresolved_identity_leads.title: Crew of Peace of Providence reported after a capture homeward from Surinam
unresolved_identity_leads.note: The scan supports the place and route, but does not name the master or connect the capture to the May Cayenne account. Keep as a possible continuation, not a confirmed second capture of the same vessel.

unresolved_identity_leads.title: Peace, Allen, of New York, reported captured from Martinique
unresolved_identity_leads.note: The port and route differ from the May account. Matching name and surname alone do not resolve vessel identity.

unresolved_identity_leads.title: Corresponding Peace/Allen/New York account appears again
unresolved_identity_leads.note: The scan repeats the Porto Rico condemnation account, with Martinico as the departure place. This is another publication, not an independent confirmation or an established continuation of the Cayenne case.
